extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners, data scientists, and finance/monetary-policy end-users interested in applying interpretable NLP to Federal Reserve communications
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and demonstrating an interpretable, no-code multi-component NLP web system (FedNLP) to analyse and visualise Federal Reserve / FOMC communications for non-programmer end-users in finance and related sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretable multi-component system
rubrics_metrics.description: FedNLP is an interpretable multi-component Natural Language Processing (NLP) system to decode Federal Reserve communications; designed for end-users to explore how NLP techniques can assist their holistic understanding of the Fed’s communications with NO coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System presents multiple NLP analyses (sentiment, prediction, explanation, summarization, topic modelling) and visualizations together so users can inspect and compare model outputs; interpretability is supported via explanation modules (e.g., LIME) and visual highlighting of contributing features/words.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-code end-user focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The system is designed for end-users (people in finance/accounting who often read economic/financial news and have low to no programming skills) to explore documents and predictions without coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver components through a lightweight web GUI and decoupled APIs so non-technical users can interact with models and custom input; define end-user requirements through preliminary focus groups to identify useful functional components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-component coverage (required NLP tasks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include multiple language processing components: sentiment analysis, topic modelling, prediction, explanation, summarization, plus demonstration features like WordCloud and counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement and present multiple components simultaneously to provide holistic views; Table 1 enumerates components and algorithms used (TextBlob, LM Sentiment, LDA, XGBoost, FinBERT, LIME, TextRank, T5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Side-by-side comparison of general vs financial-specific algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: System should show results from both general algorithms and financial domain-specific algorithms so end-users can compare their outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: general sentiment via TextBlob vs financial sentiment via Loughran-McDonald (LM) lexicon; general summarization (TextRank) vs financial abstractive summarization (fine-tuned T5); present predictions from XGBoost (general) and fine-tuned FinBERT (financial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment analysis: dual representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide both a general sentiment representation (TextBlob) and a financial-specific representation (LM sentiment) showing polarity and subjectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LM sentiment is lexicon-based built from financial documents (10-K/Q), suitable for economic/financial texts; TextBlob uses NLTK/naive-bayes for general settings — include both to assess domain sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prediction of Federal Funds Rate direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Predict the direction of changes to the Federal Funds Rate (lower, maintain, raise) by training NLP models on textual representations of FOMC decision-related documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run a suite of models (SVM, Linear SVC, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, CNN, fine-tuned BERT, fine-tuned FinBERT), evaluate using accuracy and weighted average F1, and select models based on empirical performance and class-detection behaviour (e.g., XGBoost with TF-IDF achieved test accuracy 0.73 and weighted F1 0.66 detecting all three classes; fine-tuned FinBERT overfit and only detected 'maintain' class).

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection and evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Build multiple models per task and select the final deployed models based on evaluation (accuracy, weighted F1, class detection behaviour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report numeric evaluation where available (e.g., XGBoost accuracy 0.73 / F1 0.66; FinBERT accuracy 0.72 / F1 0.65 but overfits), and use these results to choose models for the live demo (XGBoost + TF-IDF and fine-tuned FinBERT were implemented but XGBoost selected for prediction in system).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation / interpretability module
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide model explanations that are human-understandable; implementation uses Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) to visualise influential words and generate a linear surrogate model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualisation should show top contributing features and highlight sentences; consider trade-offs between fidelity and computational cost (FinBERT captures more jargon but is computationally expensive). Choose explanation/back-end models (e.g., XGBoost + LIME) and delivery optimisations to meet latency requirements (reduced explanation delivery from 10 minutes to ~30 seconds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarization: extractive and abstractive
rubrics_metrics.description: Include both extractive summarization (TextRank) and abstractive summarization (fine-tuned T5) to offer different concision and fidelity trade-offs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extractive summarization aims to capture most information with least redundancy; abstractive summarization generates new sentences to encapsulate gist. Offer both so end-users can quickly decide whether to read full content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization tailored to non-technical users
rubrics_metrics.description: Design visualisations that provide a holistic, intuitive view of document analyses (e.g., Fed Funds Rate graphs, topic modelling graphs, wordclouds, sentiment graphs, lists and filters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interface should surface key elements on landing and demo pages (financial sentiment, FFR over time, topic modelling, document lists) and allow exploration of per-document analyses; leverage proven visualization tools/ideas (e.g., What-If Tool, LIT, BertViz) but adapt for long/complex domain documents and non-developer audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web application GUI and UX principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a lightweight Angular web GUI with components for document listing, graphs, and per-document demo pages; intuitive design for end-users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modularise via page and component architecture; use six data services to access REST or NLP APIs; host as a static site on AWS S3 + CloudFront and resolve via Route 53 for ease of deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decoupled API architecture (REST and NLP APIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver components via decoupled APIs: a REST API for static/document content and an NLP API for runtime analysis tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: REST API implemented as Node.js microservices deployed on AWS Lambda and DynamoDB for static content (split endpoints for documents and document-extensions). NLP API is a Flask server inside Docker on EC2 with packaged models downloaded from S3; expose routes per NLP task to return JSON results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deployment, performance, and operational concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Operationalize models and the app with considerations for packaging, containerisation, hosting, and latency to make the demo production-like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package trained models to S3, initialise Docker environments with PyTorch/TensorFlow, use serverless microservices where appropriate, split data endpoints to improve load time, and optimise explanation delivery for acceptable user latency (example: reduced explanation time from 10 minutes to 30 seconds by using XGBoost and delivery optimisation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and domain scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and use real-world domain data from FOMC-related sources (post-meeting minutes, press releases, speeches, transcripts) across over 30 websites associated with changes in target FFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manually source metadata fields like category, domain, and author, transform and upload to DynamoDB; ensure dataset reflects the domain-specific language and decision labels (raise/maintain/lower) needed for prediction tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-centred design and requirement elicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify system requirements via preliminary focus-group interviews with target end-users to determine which functional components are most useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interviews to drive component selection and UI/UX decisions so the system addresses end-user trust (explanations), information needs (summaries, sentiment), and accessibility (no-code interface).
